title: V5 Question Types Demo
description: One question of each V5 type: Bohr shells, oxidation numbers, solubility, heating curve, gas law, molecule builder, ion builder, ionic formula and isotope mass.

questions.text: Draw the electron shells of a magnesium atom. Tap to add or remove electrons in each shell.
questions.explanation: Magnesium has 12 electrons. Shell 1 holds 2, shell 2 holds 8, and the last 2 go in shell 3.

questions.text: A gas has a volume of 2.00 L at 1.00 atm and 300 K. What is its volume at 2.00 atm and 450 K?
questions.explanation: Temperature and pressure both change, so use P₁V₁/T₁ = P₂V₂/T₂. V₂ = (1.00 × 2.00 × 450) / (300 × 2.00) = 1.50 L.

questions.text: The curve shows ice at −20 °C heated until it is steam at 130 °C. Label each numbered segment with the phase or phases present and the equation that applies.
questions.explanation: Sloped parts heat one phase (q = mcΔT). Flat parts are phase changes (q = mΔH).

questions.text: A chloride ion has a mass number of 35 and a charge of −1. Set the number of protons, neutrons and electrons it has.
questions.explanation: Chlorine has 17 protons. Neutrons = 35 − 17 = 18. Electrons = 17 + 1 = 18 (the ion gained one electron).

questions.text: Build the ionic compound that forms from aluminium and oxygen, then name it.
questions.explanation: Two Al3+ (+6) and three O2- (-6) balance, so the lowest ratio is Al2O3.

questions.text: Chlorine has two common isotopes. Use the data to calculate the average atomic mass of chlorine.
questions.explanation: Multiply each mass by its abundance as a fraction, then add: 34.969 × 0.7578 + 36.966 × 0.2422 = 35.45 amu.

questions.text: Build a molecule of carbon dioxide. Add the atoms, then join them with bonds.
questions.explanation: Carbon makes four bonds, so it forms a double bond to each oxygen. Each oxygen then has its two bonds.

questions.text: Give the oxidation number of each element in H₂SO₄.
questions.explanation: H is +1 and O is −2. The four O atoms give −8 and the two H give +2, so S must be +6 for the molecule to total 0.

questions.text: Silver nitrate and sodium chloride solutions are mixed. Mark each compound as solid (s) or aqueous (aq).
questions.explanation: Silver chloride is insoluble (s). Sodium nitrate stays dissolved (aq) because all nitrates and sodium salts are soluble. Barium sulfate is insoluble (s).
